subject: Post-call recap: SentryEdge inference constraints and deployment roadmap
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@sentryedge.com>, Priya Nair <p.nair@sentryedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Nov 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: SentryEdge inference constraints and deployment roadmap

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick written recap while items are fresh and so we have a single source of truth for next steps.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: inconsistent tail latency during peak batch scoring (promo campaign bursts) and unpredictable cost from naive scaling.
- Goal: stable 95th percentile <250ms for 1–2k daily concurrent users (target 200 QPS sustained during bursts); cost target ~50% below current on-prem GPU ops.
- Immediate asks: (1) Redwood to propose topology options (hosted + dedicated or private) with cost envelope; (2) sample traffic and model spec from SentryEdge; (3) schedule 90-min technical workshop with infra + ML engineers.

Key notes from discussion
- Workload: mix of short-answer generation (avg tokens 40–60) and reranking passes (embedding-based, 512-d). Reranks are batched and run every 5s for active sessions.
- Current infra: on-prem Titan instances (older drivers), manual autoscale. Bursts cause long queuing and 99th pct spikes.
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts; SentryEdge requires VPC/private control plane options and SOC 2 evidence.

SLOs discussed (please confirm):
- 95th percentile token latency, generation path: <= 250ms (preferred <= 200ms)
- Max cold-start latency for scale-ups: < 2s
- Throughput: baseline 100 QPS, burst to 200 QPS for 10–15 minute windows

Model / quality constraints
- Primary model family: prefer smaller quantized open models for cost (7–13B), but SentryEdge will evaluate quality vs latency tradeoffs.
- Reranking: embeddings (512-d) must be stable across quantization profiles.

Immediate next steps & owners
- SentryEdge (Alex / Priya): share 48–72h traffic sample and current perf extract (we discussed pushing perf CSV) — due EOD Thu 11/23.
- Redwood (Irene / Karthik): deliver two topology sketches (1: Hosted API with dedicated pool fallbacks; 2: Private control plane + dedicated US-West pools) + rough cost envelope — due Mon 11/27. Include SLO hit/miss scenarios.
- Schedule: propose Tue 11/28 or Wed 11/29 for 90-min deep-dive workshop — Irene to send calendar options.

Attachments referenced: request sample traffic + perf log (see action to Alex).

Thanks — I captured decisions below and will follow up with a consolidated runbook after the workshop.

—

Date: Wed, 21 Nov 2028 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SentryEdge inference constraints and deployment roadmap

Thanks Irene — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side after the call:

- The burst profile is slightly higher than we said on the call; our ops metric shows short spikes to ~250 QPS for 3–7 minutes (not sustained 15). We still want the platform to handle sustained 200 QPS for reliability planning.
- For quality: our internal QA shows regressions on paraphrase-sensitive prompts when moving below 8-bit quantization on the 13B family. We'll attach a short sample set and our perf export.

Attached: sentryedge_perf_log.csv (perf export, anonymized) — includes token-level timing and request ids.

Questions for Redwood team:
1) How would prefix/KV caching interact with our rerank pipeline? We run reranks using cached embeddings but generation prompts include dynamic session state.
2) Can you provide a back-of-envelope for cost with a dedicated pool in us-west-2 sized for 200 QPS using a rw-7b-q4 style quantized profile vs rw-13b-8bit?

We can get the traffic sample over to you by Thursday EOD as requested. Also looping in Priya to ensure security/compliance folks are prepped for the workshop.

[Attachment: sentryedge_perf_log.csv (CSV, 320KB)]

Date: Thu, 22 Nov 2028 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SentryEdge inference constraints and deployment roadmap

Alex / team — quick tech follow-up after reviewing the perf extract you sent. A few points and a proposed sketch.

Observations from perf export:
- Most high-p90/p99 events line up with queuing during burst ingress; token execution time is stable per model but queues form due to lack of continuous batching and driver-level slowdowns on older hardware.
- Rerank batching is efficient but the generation path is sensitive to prompt prefix size (we saw several sessions with prefix >200 tokens).

Proposed topology (sketch):
1) Private control plane (VPC-peered) for compliance — customer retains control plane logs and KMS; Redwood runtime sits in SentryEdge VPC or in dedicated subnet.
2) Dedicated inference pool in us-west-2 with autoscale based on request rate and active KV cache hit ratio. Use a combination of pre-warmed replicas and burstable instances to cap cold-starts.
3) Routing policy: session-affinity for active sessions (sticky to a pool node while within activity window) + fallback to hosted fallback model group in a different AZ for DR.

Model recommendations (initial):
- Primary: rw-7b-q4 (quantized 4-bit) for low-latency generation; configure 1.2x token budget to account for prefix expansion.
- Quality fallback: rw-13b-8bit for heavy-context or paraphrase-sensitive queries routed when latency SLO allows (can be configured per route).

Performance levers we will tune in workshop:
- Continuous batching window tuning (ms) to avoid queues during short bursts
- KV cache policy: cache full-turn state for active sessions; cold-key prefetch for reranks
- Operator autoscale thresholds + burst capacity sizing

Attachments: I included a redacted traffic sample we discussed.

Action items (technical):
- Redwood (Karthik): cost sketch + topology diagrams (Mon 11/27)
- SentryEdge (Alex): traffic-sample.json + QA prompt set (Thu 11/23) — confirm anonymization is OK
- Workshop: propose Wed 11/29 10:00–11:30 PST; please confirm.

[Attachment: traffic-sample.json (JSON, 48KB) — redacted request IDs]
